dates.notes: Adopted by the Heads of State and Government of the Ibero-American Community at the XXIX Ibero-American Summit in Cuenca, Ecuador, on 15 November 2024. The declaration names 18 States. It contains no signature, ratification, depositary or entry-into-force clause.

gaps: Non-binding political declaration: it creates no legal obligation, ratification, depositary, monitoring, reporting or enforcement.

The declaration names 18 States; the summit's Cuenca Declaration was adopted by 19 countries, and the Ibero-American Community has 22 members. Paraguay is not listed in this special declaration; no official explanation was located.
No full text is stored; the record is metadata-only.

Only the Spanish text was verified; no official English text was located. A Portuguese translation published by Ecuador's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is excluded because its host fails TLS certificate validation and no archived copy was located.
Implementation, follow-up and financing are not assessed.
The relationship between this declaration and the CLAD Carta Iberoamericana de IA en la Administración Pública is political, not institutional.

parties.summary: The declaration names 18 States: Andorra, Bolivia, Brasil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Ecuador, El Salvador, España, Guatemala, Honduras, Panamá, Perú, Portugal, República Dominicana, Uruguay and Venezuela. The list is reproduced from the official text; it is not a claim that the other Ibero-American States oppose the declaration.

related.note: The CLAD public-administration AI charter adopted the previous year.
The declaration builds on the Ibero-American digital-rights charter and international AI-ethics principles, including UNESCO's recommendation.
Another non-binding summit declaration on inclusive and sustainable AI.

ai_provisions: Whole declaration: ethical, trustworthy and sustainable AI for Ibero-America
Human rights, inclusion, non-discrimination and protection of vulnerable groups
Transparency, accountability, explainability and human oversight
Cooperation on AI governance, capacity building and the use of Spanish and Portuguese in AI

title.short: Ibero-American Declaration on Ethical and Trustworthy AI

checks.result: The declaration is dated Cuenca, 15 November 2024, and names the Heads of State and Government of 18 Ibero-American States. It sets out ethical, trustworthy and sustainable AI commitments and contains no treaty, signature, ratification or entry-into-force clause.

The official text lists 18 States: Andorra, Bolivia, Brasil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Ecuador, El Salvador, España, Guatemala, Honduras, Panamá, Perú, Portugal, República Dominicana, Uruguay and Venezuela. The list is reproduced exactly; Paraguay is absent.
SEGIB records the XXIX Ibero-American Summit in Cuenca on 14–15 November 2024 and 19 countries adopting the Cuenca Declaration and 24 special declarations.

verification.notes: Metadata verified from the official Ecuadorian text and SEGIB. The record is metadata-only: no full text is stored. The Spanish PDF could not be fetched automatically from this VM; the list and date were read from the official PDF as indexed and corroborated by the Portuguese official version.
